12644-through-the-iron-bars-two-years-of:
Emile Cammaerts's 1917 Through the Iron Bars, illustrated with cartoons by Louis Raemaekers, records two years of German occupation in Belgium. Contents run from prison gates and the lowered flag through poisoned wells and the sacking of Belgium. The modern slave, the creeping tide, by the waters of Babylon, and the olive branch follow.

Cammaerts notes that English readers know Belgian troops at Liège, Antwerp and the Yser, praised wherever the tale runs. Occupation, in his telling, is a prison, with gates, guards and daily humiliation. The book is wartime testimony and propaganda, vivid, angry and humane, illustrated by a cartoonist who made occupation visible to the world.
doe-osti-3000316-low-latency-quantum-con:
Marco Russo's Fermilab student report, FERMILAB-TM-2873-STUDENT, dated 16 October 2023, tests whether a neural network can steer a quantum computer's qubits. Superconducting qubits are tuned by microwave pulses, and their control electronics may one day sit in the cold beside them, where every nanosecond of delay counts. A pre-trained network promises fast, low-latency pulse choices, but only if its accuracy survives real, imperfect hardware conditions.

Russo graded the network with adapted randomized benchmarking, a routine that runs random gate sequences and scores the decay of correct answers. Simulated perturbed gates first tested the routine itself. The frozen network was then benchmarked under changed physical conditions, and finally fine-tuned, retrained gently, to recover performance. Code structure, training set design and the optimisation method are documented. The study shows a full loop: measure honestly, then adapt the model, all aimed at cryogenic control platforms.
podcast-tuckercarlson-bxFQvOyTolg:
Telegram founder Pavel Durov speaks with Tucker Carlson for the first time since his arrest in France. Carlson recalls the shock when phones lit up that August morning. Durov vanished for days with no word.

Carlson calls the arrest a turning point in how he sees Europe. He asks Durov to retell that day in full. The title calls the arrest political in motive. Durov explains the charges and his defense of free speech. The episode gives a tech founder's account of state power aimed at a private platform. His calm manner sharpens the charge he makes.
through-the-iron-bars-two-years-of-germa:
Emile Cammaerts wrote about two years of German occupation in Belgium, illustrated with cartoons by Louis Raemaekers and published in 1917. Contents name chapters on prison gates, a lowered flag, poisoned wells, and the sacking of Belgium. A final section treats modern slavery and an olive branch.

Chapter one argues English readers know Belgium's soldiers better than its civilians. One hundred thousand men checked Europe's first military empire at Liège, Antwerp, and the Yser. Readers get an occupied nation's civilian story, told to correct a picture centred only on battle.
